outcomes: A user learns from one publish --dry-run which planned members a registry would refuse, before any member is written
Every conflict of a release shows in one pass, each naming the member, the registry and the version
A dry run that could not ask a registry fails with the reason instead of passing
A member a registry already holds with the same content is reported as reused, not as a conflict
nonGoals: Knowing a registry protocol: each publisher asks its own registry, and the CLI only aggregates the records they emit
Writing to a registry, or requiring a credential for a public member
Asking for a read-only credential: a probe asks the host-only seam the real publish asks, and the cloud decides what the credential grants
Proving that a private member is absent from an answer obtained without a credential
Probing during a plan-only preview: --plan and a plan-only --dry-run execute no job

requirements.text: An executing publish --dry-run reads every member-probe event through the strict protocol reader, with or without a release-set plan. It prints one report: each conflict and unverified probe with its member, registry, version and reason, each identical member as reused with its reason, each tag-move as a warning naming the tag and both digests, and a count of absent members. The run fails once, naming every conflict, unverified and refused probe, each also as an error diagnostic. Other states pass.

With a release-set plan, each selected member no probe speaks about is reported as not probed, with its publisher and publish step or as a member whose route is unknown: a warning, never silent. A probe for a member the plan does not select, or whose version differs from the planned version, is rejected and fails the run. An absent answer obtained without a credential produces one warning, because a registry answers such a request for a private member as for a missing one.
